title: The Novena to the Holy Spirit

steps.title: Sign of the Cross
steps.versicle: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.

steps.title: Veni, Creator Spiritus (the novena's traditional opening)
Versicle and response
steps.versicle: Send forth Thy Spirit, and they shall be created:
steps.response: And Thou shalt renew the face of the earth.

veni_creator_spiritus.text:
Come, Creator Spirit,
visit the minds of your people;
fill with divine grace the hearts
which you have created.

You who are called the Paraclete,
gift of God most high,
living spring, fire, love
and spiritual anointing.

You are sevenfold in your gifts,
finger of God's right hand;
you are the Father's solemn promise
enriching our speech with power.

Kindle our senses from above,
and make our hearts overflow with love;
with patience firm and faith secure
strengthen our frail flesh.

Drive far from us our ghostly foe,
and give us your peace instead;
so shall we not, with you as guide,
turn from the path of life.

Teach us to know the Father, Son,
and you, of both, to be the love:
that through the ages all along
this may be our endless song:

Praise to your eternal merit,
Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.
Amen.
veni_creator_spiritus.latin:
Veni, creator Spiritus,
mentes tuorum visita,
imple superna gratia,
quae tu creasti, pectora.

Qui diceris Paraclitus,
altissimi donum Dei,
fons vivus, ignis, caritas,
et spiritalis unctio.

Tu, septiformis munere,
digitus paternae dexterae,
tu rite promissum Patris,
sermone ditans guttura.

Accende lumen sensibus,
infunde amorem cordibus,
infirma nostri corporis
virtute firmans perpeti.

Hostem repellas longius,
pacemque dones protinus,
ductore sic te praevio
vitemus omne noxium.

Per te sciamus da Patrem,
noscamus atque Filium;
teque utriusque Spiritum
credamus omni tempore.

Deo Patri sit gloria,
et Filio, qui a mortuis
surrexit, ac Paraclito,
in saeculorum saecula.
Amen.

veni_sancte_spiritus.text:
Come, Holy Spirit,
and send forth from heaven
the ray of your light.

Come, Father of the poor;
come, giver of gifts;
come, light of hearts.

Best consoler,
sweet guest of the soul,
sweet coolness:

In labor, rest;
in heat, refreshment;
in tears, solace.

O most blessed light,
fill the inmost heart
of your faithful.

Without your divine power,
there is nothing in man,
and nothing innocent.

Cleanse what is base,
water what is dry,
heal what is wounded.

Bend what is rigid,
warm what is chilled,
make right what is crooked.

Give to your faithful,
who trust in you,
the sevenfold gifts.

Grant the reward of virtue,
grant the deliverance of salvation,
grant eternal joy.

Amen.
veni_sancte_spiritus.latin:
Veni, Sancte Spiritus,
et emitte caelitus
lucis tuae radium.

Veni, pater pauperum,
veni, dator munerum,
veni, lumen cordium.

Consolator optime,
dulcis hospes animae,
dulce refrigerium:

In labore requies,
in aestu temperies,
in fletu solatium.

O lux beatissima,
reple cordis intima
tuorum fidelium.

Sine tuo numine,
nihil est in homine,
et nihil innoxium.

Lava quod est sordidum,
riga quod est aridum,
sana quod est saucium.

Flecte quod est rigidum,
fove quod est frigidum,
rege quod est devium.

Da tuis fidelibus,
in te confidentibus,
sacrum septenarium.

Da virtutis meritum,
da salutis exitum,
da perenne gaudium.

Amen.
veni_sancte_spiritus.source: Attributed to Stephen Langton (c. 1150-1228), Archbishop of Canterbury

schedule_note.brief_offset_correction: The brief pinned 'easterOffset startOffset -10 length 9 (ends Pentecost)': under the engine's semantics a -10 offset relative to EASTER would place the window in Holy Week, not before Pentecost. Corrected to +40: the window is Easter+40..+48 (the traditional nine days from the Friday after Ascension to the Pentecost vigil), with the divine_mercy_novena convention of a length-9 window completing ON the feast and the feast day itself not due.
schedule_note.note: The Church's oldest novena (the nine days of the apostles between the Ascension and Pentecost, Acts 1:14): from the Friday after Ascension (day 1) through the Pentecost vigil (day 9), completing on the feast of Pentecost. The tradition's per-day focus is the seven gifts of the Holy Spirit (days 1-7) carried as day variants.

variants.title: Day 1
variants.invocation: O Holy Spirit, bestow on my soul the gift of Wisdom, that I may taste how sweet Thou art and prize Thee above every created good.

variants.title: Day 2
variants.invocation: O Holy Spirit, bestow on my soul the gift of Understanding, that the mysteries of faith may shine out of my darkness.

variants.title: Day 3
variants.invocation: O Holy Spirit, bestow on my soul the gift of Counsel, that I may find Thy way in every choice and follow it at once.

variants.title: Day 4
variants.invocation: O Holy Spirit, bestow on my soul the gift of Fortitude, that with Thy strength I may carry the cross Thou choosest for me.

variants.title: Day 5
variants.invocation: O Holy Spirit, bestow on my soul the gift of Knowledge, that I may know the things that lead me to Thee and turn from them that turn me away.

variants.title: Day 6
variants.invocation: O Holy Spirit, bestow on my soul the gift of Piety, that as Thy child I may serve Thee with tenderness and joy.

variants.title: Day 7
variants.invocation: O Holy Spirit, bestow on my soul the gift of Fear of the Lord, that reverent awe may keep me from sin and near to Thee.

variants.title: Day 8
variants.invocation: O Holy Spirit, pour into my soul the fruits of Thy dwelling: charity, joy, peace, patience, kindness, and the whole harvest of Thy presence.

variants.title: Day 9
variants.invocation: O Holy Spirit, come anew into my heart on this vigil day: make the feast of Pentecost an open door for Thy gifts, and renew the face of my earth.
